headline: Discussed bridge erosion and decking repairs; listed Whipple Street roof removal and Boat Ramp table bolting as actions. No votes recorded.
summary: Members discussed erosion on the Everett Turnpike bridge trail and rot in bridge decking. They listed actions for the Whipple Street and Boat Ramp picnic tables. They also covered Trail Day cleanup projects and a running group's donation request.
decisions: Set action to remove the roof of the Whipple Street picnic table, and remove the entire table if the structure is compromised during removal. No vote was recorded.
Set action to bolt 4x4 lumber across the Boat Ramp picnic table in a Z pattern as a Trail Day project. No vote was recorded.

decision_evidence.quote: Action: Remove the roof entirely. If the structure is compromised during removal, remove the entire table. (Handled by committee/city staff, not on Trail Day, due to safety concerns.)

Action (Trail Day Project): Bolt 4x4 lumber across the tabletop in a “Z” pattern using lag bolts, washers, and lock nuts underneath. This preserves the table's function for park visitors while discouraging long-term occupation/sleeping.

plain_text:
🌲 Mine Falls Park Trail Committee 
Meeting Minutes — August 3, 2026 
Call to Order 
Steve — 7:00 PM 
Meeting Adjourned 
8:20 PM — Motion: Dave / Second: Natalie 
Attendees: Kamal Masand, Dave Silva, Ben Davis, Sherry, Mike Silva, Justin Hoprich, Steve Ke nney, Bryan Conant, 
Natalie Lucci, Andrew Lucci, Paula Lochhead. 
Minutes Acceptance (June 1st meeting): Moved by Ben, seconded by Mike. 
1. Trail & Erosion Maintenance 
Everett Turnpike Bridge / Canal Trail Erosion 
● A resident (Paul, 15 Seminole Drive) reported a deteriorating section of the tarred path near the northbound side of 
the Everett Turnpike bridge. 
● The asphalt is falling in and underpinnings are gone due to runoff from the overpass, creating a potential safety 
hazard for cyclists and pedestrians. 
● Proposed Fix: Requires a backing/form, concrete patch, and top-layer asphalt filling. Committee members will 
inspect the area to assess scope. 
2. Bridge Resurfacing & Drainage Improvements 
Weirs / Mill Pond Bridges 
● Current planks are laid parallel to the trail with minimal clearance and no crowning, causing water and debris to 
collect along the railings and rotting the wood. 
● Short-Term Actions: Investigate raising the bottom clearance of the railings so debris can slough off.  
● Long-Term Redesign: 
◦ Lay replacement wood perpendicular to the direction of travel to improve bicycle and stroller safety.  
◦ Incorporate small gaps between planks (like a residential deck) to allow proper water drainage.  
7th Street Bridge 
● Ongoing issue with rotting deck boards laid without proper spacing. 
● The committee met with the engineering department (Hoyle Tanner) to design a long -term solution. 
● Due to structural weight limits, engineering is evaluating lightweight metal decking options (e.g., expanded metal 
mesh). 
3. Unauthorized Camping & Trail Structures 
● Cove Trail Sign: Knocked over along with its cement base; needs re-installation. 
Whipple Street Picnic Table 
● Roof is severely deteriorated with holes and shingles rotting. 
● Action: Remove the roof entirely. If the structure is compromised during removal, remove the entire table. (Handled 
by committee/city staff, not on Trail Day, due to safety concerns.) 
Boat Ramp Picnic Table 
● Action (Trail Day Project): Bolt 4x4 lumber across the tabletop in a “Z” pattern using lag bolts, washers, and lock 
nuts underneath. This preserves the table's function for park visitors while discouraging long -term occupation/sleeping.
🍂 Trail Day Projects — August 15th 
Brush Cleanup, Painting, Trash Pickup, Tree Pickup near Soccer Field, Red Trail Roots Cleanup. 
📘 Facebook: As per Natalie, we have 6,000 followers on Facebook. 
🤝 Donations Request: A running group's request for donations was discussed: gloves, water, and pickers.
